svg.aria-label: Node.js 与 Git 安装向导里必须确认的选项
svg.text: Node.js installer (MSI)
Click Next throughout; pause only on this page:
Add to PATH
Makes node and npm available in any folder — keep it checked
npm package manager
npm is installed alongside Node; no separate install
Tools for Native Modules
Not needed for typical front-end work; skipping avoids a pile of build tools
Click Finish. node -v should print a version in the terminal.
If nothing happens, close and reopen the terminal (PATH is read at startup).
Git for Windows installer
Click Next throughout; only these three pages matter:
PATH environment
Choose “Git from the command line and also from 3rd-party software” (default)
Initial branch name
Choose Override and enter main — matches today's default
Line ending conversions
Keep the default (Checkout Windows-style, commit Unix-style)
The editor page is your choice; Notepad is fine and can be changed later.
You also get “Git Bash”, where most commands in this guide run.
Two things to do after installing
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
These two lines sign your commits; without them the first commit fails.
Use the same email as your GitHub account, or commits will not count toward your contribution graph.
